EBSA grants an individual prohibited transaction exemption letting a carpenters apprenticeship fund sell real property to its sponsoring council

Exemption granted · Published August 21, 2026 · Effective date not yet confirmed

The Employee Benefits Security Administration published a notice granting an individual exemption to the Mid-America Carpenters Regional Council Apprentice and Training Fund, a training trust in St. Louis, Missouri. The relief lets the fund sell real property to the Mid-America Carpenters Regional Council. The notice states that without the exemption the sale would be prohibited by ERISA.

The relief runs to this one applicant and this one transaction, so it imposes nothing on other funds. Its value to other trustees is as a reminder that a transfer of fund-owned real property to the sponsoring union or another party in interest is a prohibited transaction unless individual relief is obtained first, and that obtaining it takes an application to the Department.

The notice as published in the cluster is short. It does not give an exemption or application number, name the ERISA sections from which relief is granted, describe the property or the price, set out the conditions attached to the relief, or say whether relief extends to the excise tax under Internal Revenue Code section 4975.

The document does not state the conditions attached to the relief, the exemption or application number, or the statutory sections involved, so it cannot yet be read as a template for how the Department expects a comparable sale to be structured.

Read briefing and evidence

  • Who: The Mid-America Carpenters Regional Council Apprentice and Training Fund directly. Of reference interest to other jointly administered training trusts and welfare funds that hold real property and are considering a sale or transfer to a sponsoring union, contributing employer, or other party in interest.
  • What: No decision is required. Note the item if the fund holds real property and any transfer to a party in interest is under discussion; in that case counsel should be asked about individual exemption relief before the transaction is committed.
  • By when: No action needed now. The notice sets no deadline for other funds and states no effective date or date by which the sale must occur.
